introduction: A few principles I return to when systems, screens, or product decisions get more complex.

principles.title: Keep it simple.
principles.text: Complexity should solve a real problem. If it does not, it is probably just complexity.

principles.title: Build for the person using it.
principles.text: Technical decisions matter, but software ultimately exists to make someone’s work or life better.

principles.title: Understand before optimizing.
principles.text: Measure, find the bottleneck, then make it faster—with a reason for every change.

principles.title: Make it maintainable.
principles.text: The best decision survives the next six months, including the person who has to maintain it.
